latest_release.body:
**Release Date**: November 10, 2026
**Support Window**: Supported until May 31, 2027

> ⚠️ **Authentication changes in Rocket.Chat 9.0.0**
>
> LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth now require a premium plan, and Drupal, Facebook, LinkedIn, Meteor, X (formerly Twitter), WordPress, and Dolphin logins are removed. Community workspaces that use any of these must upgrade their plan or move users to a supported login method before updating, or those users won't be able to log in.
>
> **Supported on every plan, including Community**
>
> - Local login (username or email and password)
> - Google, GitHub, GitLab, Apple, and Nextcloud
>
> **Premium plans only (Starter, Commercial, Government, and Defense)**
>
> - LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth
>
> Eligible organizations with up to 50 users can switch to the free Starter plan.
>
> **Before you update:** make sure at least one administrator can log in with a local username and password.
>
> Preparation steps and how to recover access: [Prepare for Authentication Changes in 9.0.0](https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/prepare-for-authentication-changes-in-9-0-0)

## Summary

### Security and Compliance
_Security improvements, authentication changes, data protection, and vulnerability fixes._

MCP clients can sign in with OAuth access tokens, and private **TURN servers** for voice calls reach only users on a call. Workspace-wide ABAC enforcement adds required room attributes, ABAC-managed channels and teams, and attribute editing with a membership preview. LDAP, SAML, and custom OAuth now require a Premium license. Several built-in OAuth providers, Atlassian Crowd, anonymous write, the `query` and `fields` parameters, and the `/ufs` path are removed. Fixes cover SSRF checks for Livechat triggers, NoSQL injection, message and UiKit validation, federation checks, role permissions, 2FA email limits, and dependency updates.

### Messaging and Collaboration
_Features and fixes related to messaging, channels, discussions, and communication workflows._

Native video conference calls, powered by LiveKit, and a native XMPP server for federation are now available. Admins can control user status under **Manage** > **Workspace** > **Status and presence**. The user card and **Full profile** panel are redesigned, AI search gains filters, and the composer adds list buttons and Emoji 17.0. New workspaces start with Omnichannel turned off. Fixes improve message rendering, unread indicators, emoji sizing, client memory use, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, voice calls, and Livechat transcripts.

### Platform and Extensibility
_Developer platform, APIs, integrations, and application framework improvements._

Apps gain new UiKit blocks and elements, including `header`, `markdown`, `table`, and `video` blocks and a date-time picker. The Rocket.Chat JavaScript DDP SDK is now the official realtime SDK. REST API status codes now return 401 without a session and 403 for refused requests, and 157 deprecated DDP methods are removed. `channels.invite` accepts `userIds` and `usernames`, and the `POST /v1/push.token` response is flattened. Fixes tighten pagination and DM creation.

### Data, Storage, and Infrastructure
_Database, performance, storage, and system-level improvements._

The official Docker images move to Node.js 24.22.1 on Debian bookworm. The upgrade drops unused MongoDB indexes, and the `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` default is now 10,000 characters. Fixes improve the retention policy on large rooms, realtime updates and memory use in microservices deployments, and outbound connections after errors.

### Admin, Configuration, and Workspace Management
_Administrative controls, configuration settings, and workspace management improvements._
